description: Cookie tossing and SameSite bypass attacks — exploit browser cookie scoping rules to override, evict, or inject cookies from a sibling subdomain or via attacker-controlled responses. Chains with CSRF, session fixation, and cache poisoning.

subdomain_cookie_override.description: Sibling subdomain sets a same-name cookie scoped to the parent domain, overriding the legitimate cookie. Requires attacker-controlled content on any subdomain (XSS, subdomain takeover, or a user-content host). The tossed cookie lacks Secure/HttpOnly/__Host- prefix protections.

probes.description: Check session cookie for __Host- prefix — __Host- cookies cannot be set from a subdomain and must be Secure+path=/; absence means tossing is possible
Check if session cookie is scoped to parent domain (Domain=.example.com) — domain-scoped cookies are overridable from any subdomain

matchers.description: Cookie has explicit Domain= attribute (tossable from sibling subdomain)

samesite_lax_bypass_top_level_nav.description: SameSite=Lax cookies are sent on top-level navigation (GET) within a 2-minute window after being set. An attacker page can trigger a top-level GET to a state-changing endpoint within that window. Tests whether state-changing operations accept GET method.

probes.description: Check if Set-Cookie uses SameSite=Lax (or omits SameSite, which defaults to Lax in modern browsers)
Send state-changing endpoint as GET — if it succeeds, SameSite=Lax is bypassable via top-level navigation from an attacker page

cookie_jar_overflow.description: Browser cookie jar overflow — browsers enforce per-domain cookie limits (typically 50-180). An attacker can set many cookies from a controlled subdomain to evict the legitimate session cookie. Detection: check if the target sets more than ~30 cookies, or if a subdomain can set unlimited cookies.

probes.description: Count Set-Cookie headers in response — a high number of cookies increases susceptibility to jar overflow eviction

double_submit_cookie_bypass.description: Double-submit cookie CSRF defense bypass via cookie tossing. If the CSRF defense compares a cookie value to a body/header parameter, an attacker who can toss a cookie (from a sibling subdomain) controls both sides of the comparison.

probes.description: Check if CSRF protection uses double-submit pattern — Cookie: csrftoken=X and body/header csrftoken=X. If both match, cookie tossing breaks the defense.

matchers.description: CSRF token name in Set-Cookie header
